architecture.mechanism: The proposed architecture exploits the thermal expansion mismatch between the spindle shaft and the internal bearing, which can be mitigated by introducing a thermally stable, low-expansion material between the shaft and the bearing.
architecture.intervention: Introduce a thin, high-temperature-resistant, low-expansion ceramic coating (e.g., silicon carbide or alumina) on the spindle shaft, directly adjacent to the internal bearing. This coating will reduce the thermal expansion mismatch and minimize the thermal elongation of the spindle shaft.
architecture.expected_effect: The expected effect is a reduction in tool center point displacement by at least 50% (from 10 micrometers to 5 micrometers) during the 20-minute warmup cycle, while maintaining the required machining precision.
architecture.falsification_test: Conduct a controlled experiment with a test spindle featuring the proposed ceramic coating, and measure the tool center point displacement during a 20-minute warmup cycle. Compare the results to a baseline spindle without the coating. If the displacement is not reduced by at least 50%, the hypothesis is falsified.
